planned_outcome: Land HMS Sirius: reformulate Luikov inverse with corrected geometry — full-thickness domain x in [0, L], asymmetric BCs (radiative-convective top + conductive-tin bottom), real probe geometry (95mm T1-T8 span, 13.6mm spacing, 54mm minimum insertion). 8 free parameters. Test whether asymmetric-tin BC fixes the M13 deep-end LOO failure.
actual_outcome: Asymmetric-tin BC Luikov implemented with corrected probe geometry. Forward solver passes 4/4 sanity tests. Synthetic recovery clean: RMSE 0.49 deg C across 5 seeds, all geometry params (L, D) recover within 30 percent on 5/5 runs. Real-CSV: 4/7 converge, main-bake RMSE median 6.1 deg C — significantly improved from M11/M14 but still above 4 deg C bar. x_core_depth_inferred lands at 51-88mm physically plausible on most fixtures. T1 LOO-RMSE median 11.74 deg C — slightly improved on M9 Stefan, much better than M14 Luikov. Three fixtures hit L=137-150mm (likely upper bound near max) suggesting bound expansion needed; 100098DE landed at L=118mm, D=87mm, x_core=61.7mm — physically very plausible. Verdict CONFIRM-information-limit but materially closer than prior missions; possibly winnable with bound expansion + per-fixture tin-state metadata.
success_metric_result: Forward sanity 4/4 PASS; synthetic 8-param recovery RMSE 0.49 deg C; real-CSV main-bake RMSE 6-9 deg C (down from M14's 13-22); x_core_depth in physical range 51-88mm; T1 LOO 8.85-12.07 deg C (down from M14's 26).

adopt: Asymmetric BCs and physical probe geometry are necessary not sufficient — they cut RMSE in half but don't reach the 3 deg C bar
Synthetic 8-param recovery passes cleanly with 13.6mm sensor spacing and probe geometry baked in — the formulation IS identifiable; real-CSV failure is data-side not model-side
avoid: Reporting verdict CONFIRM purely on RMSE without contextualising the trajectory of improvement across missions
